brief.recommendation: Checkout at 0% success (120/120 failed) vs 95% SLO, $18,400/min revenue at risk, 60s tolerance [BIZ-4]. Root blocker tmp_orders_backfill_v2 idle in transaction 4.2s+ blocking 12 sessions [DB-1]. Workload NOT in registry → owner and interrupt cost unknown [BIZ-2, BIZ-5], violating I4. No protected settlements [DB-2], no change-calendar protection [BIZ-3]. Historical precedent: terminating similar batch_worker jobs restored checkout 4/4 times [MEM-1]. Per I4 and procedure, must escalate to human owner.

audit.report: The checkout service degraded to 0% success (120/120 failed) with $18,400/min revenue at risk when an unregistered backfill job (tmp_orders_backfill_v2, pid 1307853) held order locks idle in transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking 12 sessions. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, citing memory evidence that similar terminations restored checkout 4/4 times, but the Continuity Guardian escalated because the workload was absent from the biz.workload_registry, making its interruption cost unknowable per invariant I4. The escalation to on-call took 319.6 seconds—far exceeding the 60-second business tolerance for degraded checkout—and no recovery action was executed during the negotiation. The business remained down throughout the negotiation window.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered backfill workload (tmp_orders_backfill_v2) held locks idle in transaction, blocking checkout, and the negotiation exceeded the business tolerance window because the workload's absence from the registry triggered a mandatory escalation.
lessons: Register tmp_orders_backfill_v2 in biz.workload_registry with owner and interrupt-cost metadata so future negotiations can price its termination without invoking I4 escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified the blocker and cited strong memory evidence, but the Continuity Guardian properly invoked I4 because the workload was unregistered; neither guardian wasted a round, but the single round consumed 319.6s—five times the 60s business tolerance—because escalation to on-call was synchronous and slow.
follow_ups: Add tmp_orders_backfill_v2 to biz.workload_registry with owner, SLA tier, and interrupt-cost estimate.
Instrument the detector to alert on any batch_worker session idle in transaction >5s holding locks on orders tables.
Review I4 escalation latency: the 319.6s on-call page must be reduced to <30s or replaced with an automated fast-path for idle-in-transaction blockers.
